user.title: Connect to WOL Daemon
user.description: Create an API key under Settings → API keys in the daemon's web UI. With Control access you can also wake, shut down and reboot; a Read only key gives you just the status.

data_description.url: Address of the daemon's web UI, e.g. http://192.168.1.5:9090
data_description.api_key: Shown once when you create it in the daemon's settings.

reauth_confirm.title: New API key
reauth_confirm.description: The daemon at {url} no longer accepts the API key. Create a new one under Settings → API keys.

data_description.url: Address of the daemon's web UI, e.g. http://192.168.1.5:9090
data_description.api_key: Shown once when you create it in the daemon's settings.

zeroconf_confirm.title: WOL Daemon found
zeroconf_confirm.description: Found a WOL Daemon at {url}. Create an API key under Settings → API keys in its web UI and enter it here. With Control access you can also wake, shut down and reboot; a Read only key gives you just the status.

data_description.api_key: Shown once when you create it in the daemon's settings.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the daemon. Check the URL and that the daemon is up to date (it needs /api/info).
error.invalid_auth: The daemon rejected the API key.

abort.already_configured: This daemon is already set up.
abort.wrong_daemon: That's a different WOL Daemon than the one set up here.
abort.not_wol_daemon: The discovered device doesn't look like a WOL Daemon.

data_description.scan_interval: Every poll pings all machines; 30–60 seconds is plenty.
